experiment_a.finding: KG prior improves F1 by +0.0052 (from 0.863 to 0.868) at alpha=0.7 — KG lookup adds recall for known species pairs

experiment_b.finding: KG covers 4.0% of GloBI sample. Lowest recall: ENDOPARASITISM, PARASITOIDISM, SYMBIOSIS. These categories need targeted literature harvest.

publishable_commentary.strongest_finding: The 4% GloBI recall result (Experiment B) is the most publishable finding. It quantifies the gap between structured database knowledge (GloBI) and literature-extracted knowledge in a way that directly motivates the PhD work: despite focusing on host-pathogen literature, the KG recovers only 1.2% of known infection interactions from GloBI — endoparasitism recall is 0%. This is a motivation and roadmap contribution in one number.
publishable_commentary.informative_failure: SpERT trained on weak supervision achieves EP F1=0.691 vs baseline 0.868 (full_typed_a05_ner2). This tells you that the multitask model's strength is not just the architecture — it is the quality of the training signal: distilled soft labels from a large teacher ensemble over real PMC sentences, versus automated Aho-Corasick span matching over v14 CSV rows. Weak supervision alone is insufficient to displace a model fine-tuned on high-quality labels.
publishable_commentary.kg_augmentation: The KG-augmented classifier (Experiment A) shows a real but tiny gain (+0.005 F1). The signal is limited because only 1 of 100 EP-relax sentence pairs appears in the KG. If KG coverage improved from 4% to even 30%, this approach could yield a meaningful recall boost for known species pairs — making Experiment B's coverage gap finding doubly relevant: closing it would also improve the augmentation experiment.
